docs: Obama: Donald Trump tapped into a 'troubling' strain. - Obama said he recognized an "anger and fear in the American population" Athens, Greece (CNN)President Barack Obama issued a warning Tuesday against "crude nationalism" in the wake of Donald Trump's victory, saying during a news conference on his final overseas trip that the President-elect had tapped into a "troubling" strain of rhetoric playing on Americans' fears of globalization to win the presidency.

Obama Urges Donald Trump to Protect DACA Illegals. President Barack Obama said he hoped that President-elect Donald Trump would consider helping illegal immigrants brought to the United States as children who were granted amnesty by his 2012 executive order. “I will urge the president-elect and the incoming administration to think long and hard before they are endangering the status of what for all practical purposes are American kids,” Obama said. Obama’s controversial DACA and DAPA executive orders were criticized for lacking permanent protection for children of illegal immigrants and their parents, but activists were hopeful that Obama would be succeeded by a Democrat or a Republican more sympathetic to their plight. Obama defended them, asserting that they belonged in the country. “By definition, if they’re part of this program, they are solid, wonderful young people of good character,” Obama said. He suggested that the majority of Americans still supported his decision. “It is my strong belief that the majority of the American people would not want to see suddenly those kids have to start hiding again,” he said.
neutral: President Barack Obama, speaking at a news conference in Athens, Greece, during his final overseas trip as president, urged President-elect Donald Trump to "think long and hard before they are endangering the status of what for all practical purposes are American kids" protected by the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program. Obama said DACA recipients — people living in the United States illegally who arrived as children and meet certain requirements — receive work authorization and a temporary halt on deportation. "These are kids who were brought here by their parents. They did nothing wrong," Obama said. "By definition, if they're part of this program, they are solid, wonderful young people of good character." He added, "It is my strong belief that the majority of the American people would not want to see suddenly those kids have to start hiding again." Obama also warned against "crude nationalism" in the wake of Trump's victory, saying the president-elect had tapped into a "troubling" strain of rhetoric playing on Americans' fears of globalization. He said he recognized an "anger and fear in the American population." Trump made immigration a focal point of his candidacy. In a "60 Minutes" interview Sunday, he said he planned to incarcerate or deport undocumented immigrants who have committed crimes, estimating that group at 2 million to 3 million people. He said his administration would make a determination on the remaining undocumented immigrants after securing the border. "After the border is secure and after everything gets normalized, we're going to make a determination on the people that they're talking about, who are terrific people — they're terrific people, but we are going to make a determination at that," Trump said.

docs: Senator Joe Manchin Supports Jeff Sessions for AG. Time For Him To Go.. In an interview, Joe Manchin has said that he will support Jeff Sessions for Attorney General. This is now the 2nd time in 10 days that Senator Manchin has broke with party leadership, the first being when he criticized Senator Harry Reid (NV) for criticizing Trump. This is all too familiar for Democrats, as we have dealt with this many times during the years of Joe Liebermann. In my opinion, while going down to 47 seats would be unfortunate, if Manchin is going to be a part of party leadership and buck it at the same time, he is not helpful to the Democratic Party now or in 2018, where he is sure to face stiff competition in his re-elect in West Virginia. I know that party purity is not something we should strive for and is something that I don’t support in fact, but when you signal to the base of the party that you are okay with a racist, KKK supporting, homosexual bashing AG, you are no friend to Democrats or progress. It’s time for Joe Manchin to be out of party leadership and not be sent a single dime in his re-elect. Let him run as a Republican, as he seems to prefer to vote like one. Comments are closed on this story.

Democratic Sen. Joe Manchin Announces Support for Jeff Sessions as Attorney General. West Virginia’s Democratic Sen. Joe Manchin says he will vote for GOP Sen. Jeff Sessions to be confirmed as the next Attorney General. Manchin said Friday he will vote to confirm Sessions, according to The Hill. Sessions needs a simple majority in the Senate to confirm him as the nation’s next attorney general. Republicans will control 52 Senate seats by December if the GOP wins Louisiana’s special election. The former governor may face a tough re-election in 2018: His state voted for President-Elect Donald Trump with every single county voting Republican and giving him 68.7 percent of the vote. Manchin is one of several Democrats in vulnerable seats, with Democratic seats in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Florida, and Ohio also up for grabs. All five states voted Trump, with Pennsylvania turning red for the first Republican presidential candidate since 1988. Republicans could hold a filibuster-proof majority after mid-term elections if they win those 10 seats in the states which Trump won. Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell has also announced he supports Sessions for attorney general. Sessions was the first Senator to endorse Trump.
neutral: Democratic Sen. Joe Manchin of West Virginia announced Friday that he will vote to confirm Republican Sen. Jeff Sessions of Alabama as attorney general. Sessions requires a simple majority for confirmation; Republicans are expected to hold 52 Senate seats after Louisiana's runoff election next month. Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell also supports Sessions, who was the first senator to endorse President-elect Donald Trump. Manchin faces re-election in 2018 in a state where Trump won every county with 68.7 percent of the vote. Other Democratic senators up for re-election in 2018 in states Trump won include those from Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Florida and Ohio. In 1986, senators blocked Sessions from a federal judgeship after allegations — which Sessions has repeatedly denied — that he called an African-American assistant U.S. attorney "boy" and described the NAACP and the American Civil Liberties Union as "un-American." One account noted this was the second time in 10 days Manchin had broken with party leadership, citing his earlier criticism of Sen. Harry Reid for criticizing Trump, and argued Manchin should be removed from party leadership and denied re-election support because his vote signals acceptance of what that account called a "racist, KKK supporting, homosexual bashing AG."
